## Summary

Four defects in `src/papers/downloader.ts` + `src/bos/infrastructure/http/document_extractor.ts` (path traversal in filenames is clean — `sanitizeSegment` handles `../`, control chars, separators):

### 1. HTTP error statuses (401/403/404/410) treated as success (downloader.ts:342-355)

`fetchFile` returns `res.body` unconditionally; `downloadPaper` never checks `res.status`. `httpRequest` only throws on retryable statuses (408/429/5xx). Repro: an arXiv-withdrawn paper → `https://arxiv.org/pdf/<id>.pdf` returns a 404 HTML page (well over `MIN_BYTES` = 1000) → passes the size gate → the HTML branch runs link-extraction against an error page; a 403 page served as `application/octet-stream` is written to disk as a "paper".

**Fix:** `if (res.status < 200 || res.status >= 300) throw new Error('HTTP ' + res.status)` in `fetchFile` (and check status in the inner extracted-URL loop too).

### 2. Content-Type trusted over buffer magic; generic types become extensions (downloader.ts:452-457)

```ts
const format = candidate.format || contentType || detectFormatFromBuffer(buffer) || ...
```
Raw `contentType` wins over buffer magic, and `FORMAT_EXT` only maps `application/pdf`. Repro A: sci-hub candidates are chosen precisely because the probe saw `application/octet-stream` → re-fetch sees the same → `extForFormat` = `'bin'` → a real PDF saved as `.bin`. Repro B: an error body as `application/json` (≥1000 bytes) → saved as `.json`.

**Fix:** only trust a Content-Type that maps in `FORMAT_EXT` and isn't `application/octet-stream`; otherwise prefer `detectFormatFromBuffer`.

### 3. EPUB and ZIP always misdetected as DOCX (downloader.ts:46-49, 222-226)

`DOCX_MAGIC`, `ZIP_MAGIC`, `EPUB_MAGIC` are all `Buffer.from([0x50,0x4b,0x03,0x04])` and the DOCX check precedes ZIP/EPUB → the ZIP and EPUB branches are **unreachable**. Verified: every EPUB/ZIP is written as `.docx`.

**Fix:** sniff EPUB via the uncompressed `mimetype` entry near offset 30, or honor `application/epub+zip` Content-Type (possible once #2 lands); delete the duplicate constants.

### 4. `&` HTML entities not decoded before URL resolution (document_extractor.ts:118-124, used at downloader.ts:465)

`resolve()` passes the raw captured href to `new URL()`, which does not HTML-unescape. Repro: PLOS landing pages encode `href="...file?id=10.1371/journal.pone.X&type=printable"` → extracted URL keeps literal `&` → server receives param `amp;type` → returns the HTML page instead of the printable PDF → candidate rejected; download fails although a valid PDF link existed.

**Fix:** `u = u.replace(/&/g, '&')` before resolution. Note: `extractFileUrlsFromHtml` in downloader.ts:275-340 is dead code with the same flaw — delete it or route it through the fix.
title: Paper downloader: HTTP error statuses treated as success, Content-Type trusted over buffer magic, EPUB/ZIP always saved as .docx, & entities not decoded
